question: What is the primary clinical indication for inserting a permanent cardiac pacemaker?
explanation: Pacemakers are primarily indicated when the heart rate drops too low to maintain adequate blood flow, causing symptoms like dizziness and fatigue. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why is a biventricular pacemaker utilized in patients with advanced heart failure?

options.A: To continuously monitor daily fluid retention levels
options.B: To coordinate the contraction timing of both ventricles
options.C: To permanently terminate chronic atrial fibrillation
options.D: To deliver high-energy shocks for ventricular tachycardia

explanation: Biventricular pacemakers provide cardiac resynchronization therapy by pacing both ventricles simultaneously to improve pumping efficiency. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: What does a dual-chamber pacemaker system require to function properly?

options.A: Two distinct battery generators implanted on both sides of the chest
options.B: Two leads placed in the right atrium and right ventricle
options.C: External pacing pads attached continuously to the anterior chest wall
options.D: One lead threaded directly through the aorta into the left ventricle

explanation: Dual-chamber systems use two leads to monitor and pace both the upper and lower chambers of the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: In a VVI pacemaker mode, what happens when the device senses an intrinsic ventricular beat?

options.A: An immediate backup shock is delivered
options.B: Atrial contraction is forced to occur
options.C: The scheduled pacing stimulus is inhibited

explanation: Inhibit modes withhold the pacing impulse if the heart beats on its own within the programmed time window, preventing competition with native rhythms. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why is hair clipping preferred over shaving at the surgical site before pacemaker insertion?

options.A: Clipping prevents microscopic skin abrasions that harbor bacteria
options.B: Shaving interferes with the adhesive properties of surgical drapes
options.C: Clipping takes significantly less time for operating theatre staff
options.D: Shaving permanently damages the underlying superficial nerve pathways

explanation: Razors cause tiny cuts in the skin where bacteria can multiply, increasing the risk of pocket site infection. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the nurse during pre-procedural medication reconciliation?

options.A: Stopping all oral cardiac medications permanently prior to surgery
options.B: Ensuring all routine daily antibiotics are doubled in dosage
options.C: Administering high-dose sedatives on the general medical ward
options.D: Checking for anticoagulants that might increase bleeding risks

explanation: Anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents must be identified because they increase the risk of hematoma formation at the surgical pocket site. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which diagnostic imaging test is routinely ordered immediately after pacemaker insertion to check for complications?
explanation: A chest radiograph is performed immediately post-procedure to verify lead placement and ensure a pneumothorax did not occur during insertion. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: A patient returns to the ward after pacemaker insertion. Which nursing action is most critical for preventing lead dislodgement?

options.A: Encouraging immediate range-of-motion exercises for both upper extremities
options.B: Massaging the subcutaneous pocket site gently every four hours
options.C: Restricting movement of the affected arm and avoiding elevation above the shoulder
options.D: Positioning the patient flat on their back with the head completely lowered

explanation: Limiting movement of the arm on the operative side prevents pulling on the newly placed leads before tissue ingrowth secures them. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: How long must a patient generally avoid lifting the affected arm above shoulder level after pacemaker insertion?
explanation: It takes several weeks for the pacemaker leads to become firmly anchored by scar tissue inside the heart wall. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why should a patient avoid soaking the surgical incision in water during the initial post-operative healing phase?

options.A: Moisture softens the incision line and promotes bacterial migration
options.B: Moisture neutralizes the antiseptic ointment applied in theater
options.C: Submersion causes the titanium casing to rust and corrode rapidly
options.D: Water pressure can instantly reprogram the device generator settings

explanation: Keeping the wound dry prevents infection and protects the integrity of the closing skin sutures or staples. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: What electrocardiographic pattern defines pacemaker failure to capture?

options.A: Pacing spikes visible without a resulting myocardial depolarization complex
options.B: Continuous firing of rapid pacing spikes at rates exceeding 200 beats per minute
options.C: Pacing spikes landing directly on top of native T waves
options.D: Complete absence of any visible electrical pacing spikes on the monitor

explanation: Failure to capture means the electrical energy delivered by the generator is not strong enough or the lead is displaced, resulting in a spike without a heartbeat. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which complication occurs when a pacemaker mistakenly identifies skeletal muscle electrical activity as a natural heartbeat and withholds pacing?
explanation: Oversensing happens when extraneous electrical signals are interpreted as native heartbeats, causing the pacemaker to inappropriately skip programmed pacing. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: How should a patient with a pacemaker navigate airport security screening safely?

options.A: Show the device ID card and request a manual hand-wand or pat-down search
options.B: Remove the implanted device temporarily and place it in carry-on luggage
options.C: Turn off the pacemaker generator completely before entering the security queue
options.D: Walk rapidly through standard magnetic archway detectors without stopping

explanation: Airport security metal detectors and wands can temporarily interfere with pacemaker settings, so manual screening is recommended. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following household items poses the least risk of interference to a modern pacemaker?
explanation: Modern microwave ovens are well-shielded and do not emit electromagnetic fields strong enough to interfere with properly functioning pacemakers. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of routine pacemaker interrogation during follow-up visits?

options.A: Surgically replacing the entire generator unit during an outpatient visit
options.B: Clearing scar tissue buildup surrounding the subcutaneous pocket
options.C: Checking battery status, lead impedance, and device programming
options.D: Reprogramming the heart muscle to beat at a permanently fixed rate

explanation: Interrogation evaluates technical performance parameters like battery life and lead integrity to ensure the device is working optimally. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: Which intervention best addresses the emotional and psychosocial needs of a patient newly fitted with a pacemaker?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on technical maintenance while ignoring emotional cues
options.B: Discouraging the patient from discussing their device fears with family members
options.C: Assuring the patient that lifestyle restrictions will remain permanent and strict
options.D: Providing structured education, active listening, and referral to support resources

explanation: Addressing anxiety and body image concerns through supportive counseling aids successful psychological adjustment to the device. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)
